chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I asked a man by the Face of Allah, so he whipped me with five lashes.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) whipped him with five other lashes and said, 'Ask by your own ignoble face.'
ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette of asking someone by the Face of Allah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Prophet’s practical application of *qisas* (retributive justice) by mirroring the exact punishment inflicted, while simultaneously critiquing the social etiquette of invoking authority through 'the Face of Allah' in casual disputes. Shia scholars often interpret the phrase 'ask by your ignoble face' as a reminder that the dignity of the requester matters as much as the dignity of the one being asked, emphasizing humility in social transactions.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘A man came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! I asked a man by the Face of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so he whipped me five lashes’. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> whipped him another five lashes and said: ‘Ask by your own ignoble face’.
